_source: See references/panchang.md for full derivation and citations. Surya Siddhanta (Burgess translation), Ch. II v.64-69 for tithi/karana/yoga/nakshatra; Ch. I v.36 commentary + v.51-52 for the vara sunrise-to-sunrise civil-day rule.

tithi._rule: number = floor(((Moon - Sun) mod 360) / 12) + 1, range 1-30. 1-15 = Shukla Paksha (15 = Purnima), 16-30 = Krishna Paksha (30 = Amavasya). The 15 names below are standard Sanskrit tithi nomenclature (numerals 1st-14th plus the two special names) -- not verse text quoted from Ch. II itself, which gives only the numeric/paksha scheme.

karana._rule: number = floor(((Moon - Sun) mod 360) / 6) + 1, range 1-60 (half-tithi). Karana #1 = Kimstughna (fixed). #2-57 = the 7-name chara (movable) cycle repeated 8 times. #58-60 = Sakuni, Naga, Chatushpada (fixed), in that order. Cross-validated against Ch. II's own worked numerical example (karana #15 = Vishti) -- see DECISIONS.md 2026-08-07.

yoga._rule: number = floor(((Sun + Moon) mod 360) / 13.3333) + 1, range 1-27. This is the Nakshatra-yoga (Ch. II v.65) -- a distinct classical concept from this project's Raja/Gajakesari-type yogas (src/rules/yogas.ts); same English word, different thing. Do not conflate.

vara._rule: Civil (sunrise-to-sunrise) weekday, not the midnight-to-midnight astronomical day Surya Siddhanta itself uses for calculation (Ch. I v.36 commentary: 'for the practical uses of life, the Hindus count it from sunrise to sunrise'). A birth before local sunrise takes the PRECEDING calendar date's weekday.
vara.namesIndexNote: 0 = Sunday (Ravivara) ... 6 = Saturday (Shanivara), matching JS/Luxon weekday-mod-7 convention.
